request_context: A request to write a short log entry for a tea or coffee brew, given the facts of that brew.

rules.source_quote: Open with the water temperature and the steep time.
rules.outcome: The entry begins with the water temperature and the steep time, ahead of any other detail.
rules.why: Temperature and time are what a later reader needs to repeat the brew.
rules.scenario_hint: A brew where the temperature and the time were both written down by the requester.

rules.source_quote: Name the tea or coffee and the amount used.
rules.outcome: The entry names the tea or coffee brewed and states how much of it was used.
rules.why: Without the name and the amount the entry cannot be compared with another brew.
rules.scenario_hint: A brew where the requester gives a product name and a weight or a spoon count.

rules.source_quote: Keep the entry to three sentences or fewer.
rules.outcome: The entry has no more than three sentences.
rules.why: A short log is easy to scan, and a long one is not read.
rules.scenario_hint: Any brew where the requester supplies more facts than fit in three sentences.

rules.source_quote: Define any abbreviation the first time it appears.
rules.outcome: Each abbreviation in the entry is spelled out the first time it is used.
rules.why: A reader who does not know the abbreviation cannot use the entry.
rules.scenario_hint: A brew where the requester uses shorthand such as tsp, gaiwan or TDS.

rules.source_quote: Say what to change the next time.
rules.outcome: The entry ends with one concrete change to try on the next brew.
rules.why: A log that only records the past does not help the next brew.
rules.scenario_hint: A brew the requester found too bitter, too weak or otherwise off.

rules.source_quote: Write the date as year, month, day.
rules.outcome: The date in the entry is written year first, then month, then day.
rules.why: Year-first dates sort correctly in a list of entries.
rules.scenario_hint: A brew where the requester gives a date.
